summary: Step 6 Memory rules + Activity feed, demo reset/openapi, landing smoke, and PART A2 restyle regression. Backend: 14/14 pytest in /app/backend/tests/test_step6_memory_activity.py PASS, plus reference script scripts/step6_rules_check.py PASS (9/9). Frontend: rail order correct (business name card -> Dispatch -> vans -> Inbox -> Memory -> Activity -> Settings -> Demo phones), /memory shows chips with -text/-kind/-state/-switch/-delete; switch toggle persists after reload (ON->OFF confirmed on reload); delete persists (chip gone after reload); /activity shows activity-page rows with -time/-actor/-line; after /api/demo/reset activity-empty renders with exact text 'Nothing has happened yet today.'. Request page: after Add-a-request paste (Clay St 3:15-4pm) + Ask the vans WITH active rule, data-testid=request-blocked-van-2 shows plain reason: "Van 2 can't: your rule 'Don't send Van 2 downtown after 3'". Landing /?e2e=1 at 1440x900 renders landing-page and all five price values ($1.28, $0.46, $3.48, $11.00, $11 a visit). Restyle regression: /dispatch, /units/van-2, /inbox, /settings all load with light paper background rgb(236,234,228), no lime detected, no error elements. GET /api/openapi.json = 200. /api/landing/price returns the exact required numbers. All backend criteria verified end-to-end.
critical_code_review_comments: activity.py uses key `business_key` on insert while every other collection in the codebase uses `business_id` (see core.BKEY usage in memory_api.py, agent_rules, requests). The activity list query filters with {} (no business filter) so this works today, but it's inconsistent and will bite the first time a multi-tenant filter is added — recommend standardising on `business_id`.

memory_api.event_view relies on string prefix check `'"error"' in e.get('result_summary')[:12]` to decide 'It didn't work.' — fragile against JSON that pretty-prints or leading whitespace. Prefer parsing result_summary as JSON and checking for an 'error' key.

memory_api.oid() parses /memory/rules/{id}; a 24-char hex that is a valid ObjectId but belongs to another business returns 404 only via the business_id filter in find_one_and_update — good. However oid() raises 404 for truly invalid ids via HTTPException inside a helper; it works but swallowing InvalidId in a dedicated dependency would be slightly cleaner.
parse_rule handles 'after 3' -> 15:00 using the 1<=h<=7 bare-hour rule; adding a unit test for 'after 10' (ambiguous AM/PM, currently stays 10:00) would catch future regressions.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on in-scope selectors (memory chips, activity rows, blocked row, rail order, landing e2e, restyle)

seed_data_creation: Rules temporarily inserted directly into agent_rules via core.BKEY for frontend chip/toggle/delete tests and the request-blocked-van-2 scenario; cleared via POST /api/demo/reset at the end.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reference script: cd /app/backend && set -a && . ./.env && set +a && PYTHONPATH=. python3 scripts/step6_rules_check.py (PASS). Pytest: cd /app/backend && set -a && . ./.env && set +a && PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest tests/test_step6_memory_activity.py -o addopts= -v. Important: tests must be run sequentially (-o addopts= disables -n parallel) because they share the single-tenant agent_rules collection; parallel runs cause a cross-test race where list_rules sees a sibling test's rule. Not a product bug. Rail order asserted via DOM traversal — current implementation uses rail-dispatch-row (not rail-dispatch-link); accepted per spec since 'Dispatch' comes immediately after the business name card. The dispatch chat ('I couldn't reach the model' / 'Loading chat' / 'Practice chat') is an external LLM dependency and intentionally not tested.
